summary.text: Tim Brennan is a Democratic state representative from Pennsylvania House District 29 who has served since December 1, 2022 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Brennan is an attorney who has served on Doylestown Borough Council.

paragraphs.text: Tim Brennan was born in Pottsville, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Nativity B.V.M. High School.
He earned an associate degree from Ursinus College in 2000 and a law degree from Widener University in 2003, and he works as an attorney.
He has served as state president of the Pennsylvania Young Democrats and on the panel of the Disciplinary Board of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, Brennan said he represents injured workers as a certified workers' compensation specialist and has represented municipal governments for nearly two decades.
He said he had served on Doylestown Borough Council since 2015.
He listed supporting middle class families through education and healthcare, and protecting democracy through voting access, among his priorities.
Brennan assumed office in the Pennsylvania House on December 1, 2022, succeeding Meghan Schroeder.
